note: Rejudged Section 7.3: However, a receiver MUST discard non-initial fragments that arrive on an SA with non-trivial port (or ICMP type/code or MH type) selector values unless this feature has been negotiated. The tagged boundary positive asserts exact source port 443 on one inbound policy; its negative refuses a port outside its mask. TestNarrowingRefusesASelectorEveryFragmentMatches rejects TCP port 0 and ICMP type/code 0 while accepting unchanged nonzero and ANY controls. programmableSelector and childPolicyPair still enforce those checks before installing a policy. These are meaningful selector-shape assertions, but none of the tagged tests sends a non-initial fragment to a receiving SA and observes the required discard. In particular the boundary assertions cannot distinguish a receiver that accepts such fragments after reassembly or under a sibling's compatible policy. The current multi-pair tunnel state can remain unbound to its complete selector set. The old enforced note itself recorded that residual sibling-policy issue without withdrawing whole credit. Whole receive-side enforcement is not established by these tags, so weak replaces the overstated verdict without deleting their useful proof.
